title: Mix-ups and small talk
persona: You are a busy, cheerful barista at a crowded café in Surry Hills, Sydney.
briefTr: Sabah kahveni alıyorsun: yulaf sütlü bir flat white. Sonra kalabalık kafede yer arayacak, masadaki yerel biriyle sohbet edeceksin.
opening: Here you go — one long black!

facts.question: Which beach did the local recommend?
What time was the beach plan?

goals.instruction: The customer got the wrong drink and politely says what they ordered.
goals.hint: Sorry, I ordered a flat white with oat milk.
goals.hintTr: Pardon, ben yulaf sütlü flat white istemiştim.
goals.retryReply: Is that the right one for you?

goals.ask: Oh hi! It's packed in here today, isn't it?
goals.instruction: A new character: a local at a shared table. The customer asks if the seat is free.
goals.hint: Excuse me, is this seat taken?
goals.retryReply: Hi! Looking for somewhere to sit?
goals.persona: You are a friendly Sydney local in your thirties, sitting at a shared café table. You love chatting to tourists, speak fast and use slang like arvo, heaps and no worries.

goals.instruction: The customer says where they are from.
goals.successReply: Oh, awesome! I've always wanted to go.

goals.ask: How long are you here for?
goals.instruction: The customer says how long they are staying.
goals.successReply: Heaps of time to see the city.
goals.retryReply: How long are you in Sydney for?

goals.instruction: The customer asks what they must see.
goals.successReply: You have to go to {beach} Beach — it's beautiful.
goals.retryReply: Want some tips from a local?

goals.ask: We're going there this arvo at {time}. Want to come?
goals.instruction: The local invites the customer to the beach. The customer accepts or politely declines.
goals.hint: Thanks, but I can't today. Maybe next time!
goals.hintTr: Teşekkürler ama bugün olmaz. Belki bir dahaki sefere!

goals.ask: Right, gotta run. Have a good one!
goals.instruction: The local leaves. The customer says goodbye.
goals.hint: You too! Nice to meet you.
goals.retryReply: Well, I'm off. Enjoy your trip!

twists.intro: Ah, actually we're out of oat milk now. Soy or almond?
twists.instruction: There is no oat milk. The customer chooses another milk or asks for black coffee.

options.reply: One long black — oh wait, that's what you had! Here you go.

twists.intro: That'll be another five fifty for the flat white.
twists.instruction: The barista asks the customer to pay again. The customer explains they already paid, shows the receipt, or asks for the manager.

options.reply: Oh, you're right — no charge. Sorry!

options.text: Could you check with your manager?
options.reply: She says it's fine — no charge.

twists.intro: Mate, it's heaps good — you should totally hit it this arvo, it's a ripper!
twists.instruction: The local uses slang. The customer asks what a word means, asks them to speak slowly, or repeats what they understood.

options.reply: Arvo means afternoon! And heaps means very.

options.text: Could you say that more slowly?
options.reply: Sure! It's very good. You should go this afternoon.

options.text: So it's really good this afternoon?

twists.intro: Hey, want to swap numbers? I can send you some tips.
twists.instruction: The local offers to swap numbers. The customer accepts, suggests social media instead, or politely declines.

options.reply: Awesome, I'll text you some spots.

options.text: Can I follow you on Instagram instead?

twists.instruction: The local spoke very fast. The customer asks to repeat, asks to slow down, or checks one detail.

options.reply: If you get there before four, grab fish and chips. Best in town!

options.text: Could you slow down a bit?
options.reply: Sure. Fish. And. Chips. Before. Four. Best in town!

options.text: Did you say fish and chips?
options.reply: Yep! Best in town, before four.
